resources.string: Formats a stick as FAT32 (MBR), the way Pioneer players such as the XDJ-700 read it. Formatting erases everything on the stick.
Connect a USB stick with an OTG adapter. It appears here as soon as it is plugged in.
This device\'s storage protocol is not supported (for example, USB Attached SCSI only).
Sonora needs permission to use %1$s before it can format it.
Up to 11 characters: English letters, digits, spaces and simple symbols.
Fix the volume label to continue.
This stick is write-protected, so it can\'t be formatted. Slide its lock switch off, or use another stick.
ALL data on \"%1$s\" will be erased. The stick will be formatted as FAT32 (MBR) for Pioneer players, with the label %2$s.
Keep the stick connected. The screen stays on until formatting ends.
Formatting can\'t be left with Back. Use Cancel to stop it; the stick then has to be formatted again.
If the stick doesn\'t appear in Android, unplug and replug it.
Enter a label of 1 to %1$d characters.
The label has %1$d characters; FAT allows at most %2$d.
\"%1$s\" is not allowed in a FAT label.
\"%1$s\" is not allowed: use English letters, digits, spaces and simple symbols.
Sonora was not allowed to use this USB device.
The USB stick was disconnected while formatting. Plug it in again and format it before using it.
The USB stick was already released. Select it again.
This device can\'t be formatted here: %1$s.
No medium found. Insert a card into the reader, or use another stick.
The USB stick stopped responding. Unplug it, plug it in again and retry.
The stick rejected a command (sense key 0x%1$X, ASC 0x%2$02X, ASCQ 0x%3$02X). Try another stick.
The USB stick could not be used: %1$s.
This stick holds %1$s, too little for a FAT32 volume. Nothing was written.
This stick holds %1$s, more than the %2$s an MBR partition can describe. Nothing was written.
This stick uses %1$d-byte blocks; Sonora formats sticks with 512 or 4096-byte blocks. Nothing was written.
The stick refused to be written. The stick must be formatted again before it can be used.
The stick failed at block %1$d. %2$s The stick must be formatted again before it can be used. If this keeps happening, the stick may be faulty.
The stick failed while saving its cache. %1$s The stick must be formatted again before it can be used. If this keeps happening, the stick may be faulty.
The %1$s at block %2$d read back differently from what was written. This stick does not store data reliably (it may be faulty or counterfeit); don\'t use it for music.
Formatting stopped before it finished. The stick is not usable until it is formatted again.
Something went wrong while formatting. The stick must be formatted again before it can be used.
Copies tracks to a stick with a rekordbox library, so the %1$s shows their waveforms, beat grids and keys. It takes %2$s; anything else is converted to that on the way.

Add audio files, or a folder of them.

resources.string: Pick the USB stick itself (prepare it above first). Android asks once for access to it.
Connected stick: %1$s. Choose it once to give Sonora access; after that it opens by itself.
Several storage devices are connected. Choose the USB stick:
Eject %1$s in Android\'s settings (Eject or Unmount), then come back. Sonora shows here when it can be unplugged.
Eject the stick in Android\'s settings (Eject or Unmount), then come back. Sonora shows here when it can be unplugged.
Android\'s storage settings couldn\'t be opened. Eject the stick from its notification or in Settings > Storage; Sonora shows here when it can be unplugged.
The stick can be unplugged now.
The exported tracks also go into this playlist; an existing one gets them added. Leave it empty for none.
Not enough space: the export needs about %1$s and the stick has %2$s free.
Replace the library on this stick?
Keep the stick connected. You can leave Sonora meanwhile; the export goes on.
Sonora can\'t read this file. It may have been moved or deleted.
Sonora can\'t read this folder. It may have been moved or deleted.
Sonora can\'t decode this audio (%1$s), so it can\'t convert it for the %2$s.
Android didn\'t let Sonora keep access to this storage. Pick the stick again and allow access.
This storage can\'t be used. Unplug the stick, plug it in again and pick it once more.
Pick the top level of the USB stick (its name, not a folder on it): the player only looks there.
Another export is still running. Wait for it to finish, then export again.
No rekordbox library yet: the export creates one.

resources.string: A rekordbox library made by another app. Exporting replaces it.
A library from a newer version of Sonora. Update Sonora, or exporting replaces it.
Sonora\'s library record on this stick is damaged. Exporting replaces the library.

This stick has a rekordbox library that Sonora didn\'t make. Exporting replaces it with a new library holding only the tracks you export now. The other music files stay on the stick, but the player won\'t list them, nor their playlists, cues or analysis.

The library on this stick can\'t be read. Exporting replaces it with a new library holding only the tracks you export now. The other music files stay on the stick, but the player won\'t list them, nor their playlists, cues or analysis.

resources.string: Eject the stick in Android before unplugging it.
No track could be added; the stick was not changed.
The export needs about %1$s; the stick has %2$s free. Nothing was written.
The library on this stick would be replaced. Start the export again and confirm.
The export stopped while the stick\'s library was being written, so the player may not list everything. Plug the stick in again and export again: that completes the library.
The stick failed (it may have been unplugged or be full). Its library is as it was before this export.
The export stopped on an unexpected problem (Copy technical details shows it). The stick\'s library is as it was before this export.
The stick\'s library is as it was before; the files this export had copied were removed.
